meta.scope: FINAL EXTERIOR PRESENTATION REALISM: material node trees (same names, same slot assignments), world/sky, colour management, render settings and validation cameras only. Every vertex, transform, collection, face material index and material slot is hash-verified identical to v012. No geometry, no plant, no grade, no signage, no people, no vehicles, no interiors.
meta.colour_space: linear RGB (Blender base colour); tones derived from the documented products (v002 material control) and checked against the genuine photographs 2025-09-09 and 2026-07-28; placeholders keep their v002 tones
meta.units: metres in node space (Blender units); brick module 12 in x 4 in course = 0.3048 x 0.1016 m incl. 3/8 in joints = 0.0095 m
meta.evidence_codes: W written (legend/schedule), C closeout product record, P photo-consistent (genuine photos 2025-09-09 / 2026-07-28 / 2026-08-10, validation only), I interpreted shading value, A assumed (module/spacing not documented), U unresolved placeholder
meta.panel_patterns: A4.02 Material Legend: PNL1 = Panel Type 1 (Vertical Pattern) flush wall panels; PNL2 = Panel Type 2 (Grid Pattern) with vertical and horizontal 3/4 in reveal seams; PNL3 = Panel Type 3 (Horizontal Pattern) flush and reveal (unresolved placeholder, no pattern applied). Seam WIDTH 3/4 in is written (W); seam PITCH is not documented anywhere in the set or closeout -> assumed (A): PNL1 vertical seams every 2.0 ft, PNL2 grid 4.0 x 2.0 ft. Seams are shader bumps only (no geometry).

sky.rotation_convention: test scene 2026-09-23: 0 deg = sun from north (+Y), 90 deg = from east (+X); 75 deg = from the east-north-east, elevation 42 deg = a clear summer morning in Charlotte, chosen so the north entrance face receives grazing sun and the east face full sun (the v001 validation sun came from the south-west and left the front in shade) | v013: elevation raised 42 -> 47 deg (late-morning, softer shadow length, neutral architectural-photography daylight); rotation unchanged

ground_below_horizon.note: world shader only: below the horizon the physical sky is dark; a neutral matte ground tone is shown there so views that look past the modeled terrain do not fall into black. Not geometry, not context. Strength 20 chosen from trials (10/25/60): reads as a neutral mid-light grey close to the sunlit lawn/walk tones.

view.exposure_basis: v009 calibration (18 % grey reads 0.47 at -5.0); -4.35 after v013 trial renders with the brighter sky (elevation 47) and the coated ACM: no clipped highlights, shaded north face mid-tone

render.note: 384 samples with adaptive sampling; OptiX denoise; caustics off; indirect clamp 10; no DOF, no motion blur, no look/grading
